title: daybench-snapshot-clara
content:
Purpose: quick personal ledger for small microbench runs I can run on my dev box or a small dedicated slot. Not formal bench, just a compact reference for tradeoffs (batch vs latency vs cost).

Context/notes to self:
- Morning quick-runs: want simple reproducible rows I can re-run during the week.
- Focus: short sequences (64-512) and bursty small batches (1-8) because product calls are chat-like.
- Keep cost calc in the same doc so I don’t forget conversion factors.

Quick table (rows = single run snapshot) — columns: id | date | model | seq | batch | p50_ms | p95_ms | cost_per_1k_tokens_usd | notes

1 | 2024-04-28 | redwood-instruct-3b-8bit | 64 | 1 | 48 | 78 | 0.0012 | baseline single-shot, no prefix cache, CPU fallbacks hit once
2 | 2024-04-28 | llama2-13b-chat-8bit | 64 | 1 | 112 | 170 | 0.0026 | good quality, p95 high on small GPU due to mem swap
3 | 2024-04-29 | gptj-6b-4bit | 128 | 2 | 95 | 160 | 0.0010 | batching helps p50 but p95 stays noisy
4 | 2024-05-03 | falcon-7b-instruct | 256 | 4 | 210 | 360 | 0.0018 | seq growth dominates, try kv cache next run
5 | 2024-05-09 | redwood-instruct-3b-8bit | 512 | 8 | 870 | 1100 | 0.0020 | big seq+batch -> memory pressure, consider quant profile B

Quick calculations / helpers:
- cost_per_1M_tokens = cost_per_1k_tokens_usd * 1000
  example: 0.0012 per 1k -> 1.2 USD per 1M tokens
- latency amortization rough: p50_total_tokens = (seq * batch) ; treat p50_per_token ~ p50_ms / seq (very rough)

Scratch calcs (today):
- run #1: p50_per_token ~ 48ms / 64 = 0.75 ms/token -> for a 32-token reply ~ 24 ms token-only
- run #4: p50_per_token ~ 210 / 256 = 0.82 ms/token (similar per-token, overheads different)

Notes / quick hypotheses:
- Batching yields diminishing returns beyond 4 for my dev slot; p95 becomes dominated by memory and occasional GC.
- 8-bit quant gives decent p50 improvements but p95 varies by model/kernel.
- For chat UX, latency tail matters more than mean for 95% of requests; aim to keep p95 < 300ms for seq<=128, else degrade UX.

To-run (short checklist):
- [ ] re-run run#2 with kv-cache=true and measure p95 (JIRA INF-789 reminds me to check cache warm-up)
- [ ] try quant profile B on redwood-instruct-3b for seq=512 run (expect lower memory)
- [ ] test batch=3 and batch=5 for gptj-6b to find knee point

Quick run commands (saved snippets) — dev slot commands I use:
- local run minimal: ./bench --model redwood-instruct-3b --seq 64 --batch 1 --profile perf 
- with kv cache: ./bench --model redwood-instruct-3b --seq 128 --batch 2 --kv-cache --trace

Open questions / followups:
- Is the p95 variability due to my small GPU host (swap/drive) or kernel selection? Compare identical runs on dedicated slot.
- Cost calc: confirm token accounting with the recent tokenizer changes (ticket in GH PR above).

Short log (morning):
- 2024-05-11 09:20 — ran quick batch sweep on dev; saw p95 spikes on falcon after 2nd run; suspect mem fragmentation. Filed quick note on Slack #infra with logs.

Short log (evening):
- 2024-05-11 18:05 — re-ran redwood-3b with quant profile B; memory stable, p50 down ~8%, p95 down ~10% (promising). Save config to experiment branch.

Next steps (week):
- Consolidate promising configs into a small smoke-check script and push to my fork under runtime/bench/quick-smoke.
- If stable, propose a tiny perf note for the internal perf digest (1 paragraph).

Random notes to self:
- When in doubt, snapshot kernel logs (/tmp/kernel-alloc.log) immediately after p95 spike.
- Keep this doc lightweight — copy into a proper shared drive note if I intend to escalate.

End of daybench snapshot.
